messages.author: 2c646f60b794c4b1
messages.subject: DATA FILTER error
parts:
Dear Distance-Samplers,

I have an interesting error which I hope to solicit a solution for. I am
analyzing marine mammal line transect data and using the
POST-STRATIFICATION option (by SPECIES from the observation layer) combined
with the DATA FILTER to create subsets of my data. In using the DATA
FILTER, I am selecting only one cluster size category (CS<=25 from the
OBSERVATION layer) and one season (= 1 or 2, from the LINE TRANSECT layer).
When I select one season and cluster size and post-stratify by species,
the analysis runs fine. I encounter a problem when I try to select both
seasons (SEASON <=2) with all other parameters unchanged. The data type of
the SEASON field is integer, so I don't think there's a problem with the
operator <=2. Distance gives the following error:

"An error occurred within the analysis engine. This could be due to a
problem in the Distance analysis engine, or could be because the analysis
was reset just as it was finishing."

I would be interested in hearing from anyone else who has encountered this
problem.

Jim Carretta

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: DATA FILTER error
parts:
Jim (and anyone else with this problem),

Thanks for sending me the test project. Your problem is that you are running
an analysis with more than 5000 samples (transects). The analysis engine
that comes with Distance 3.5 can only cope with 5000 samples and 10000
observations. You need to download and install the large-dataset version of
the analysis engine - you can get this from the distance web site, under
"Support, Updates and Extras". Then everything should run fine.

You may not have realized that you were running more than 5000 samples, since
your dataset contains only 474 transects. However, in your problematic
analysis you post-stratify by species, and there are 11 species. When you
post-stratify by a field in the observation layer, Distance duplicates your
samples once for each post-stratum level; in your case 474x11=5214.

Also, Distance didn't give you a very informative error message (it should
have said something like "Too many samples"). Sorry about that! Your
dataset enabled me to discover a minor bug in the analysis engine which means
that instead of exiting gracefully when there are too many samples it crashes
out. The Distance interface therefore doesn't know what the problem was and
gives you the generic message "** Error: An error occurred within the

analysis engine. This could be due to a problem in the Distance analysis
engine, or could be because the analysis was reset just as it was finishing.

**". We'll have this problem fixed in future releases of Distance.

I've added a note to the "Known Problems" page on the web site in case anyone
else gets a similar problem in the future.

As you said, you have a fairly complex dataset, with geographic, group size,
seasonal and species strata. Hopefully, Distance 4 will deal with such
complex situations better than 3.5. For one thing it will cope with multiple
levels of stratification. For another I'm going to expand the data selection
to allow more complex queries. However, for now, you may find yourself
having to split your dataset out into separate distance project - e.g., one
project for each species.

All the best,

- Len Thomas
